$comment: AUTHORITY for what a registry of knowledge bases does with the resources open in a knowledge base when a session with it becomes active: it asks the knowledge base to describe itself, reads the answer against the entry it was asked as (protocol/specs/src/client/registry.json's KbReadVerdict), and checks each resource open in it (TabCheck). Every SDK runs every case against its own registry over a scripted knowledge base, and fails on a difference. A verdict of no verdict (the knowledge base did not answer, or could not say who it is) is evidence of nothing: every open resource is checked, exactly as when the knowledge base answered as its entry. Only a resource the knowledge base says is gone (`bus.not-found`) closes; one it describes stays, and so does one it gave no answer about, since a fault is no verdict. READING A CASE. `kb` is what the knowledge base answers when asked to describe itself: `itself`, the did of the entry it was asked as; `unanswered`, nothing. `open` is the ids of the resources open in it before the session is active. `resources` is what it answers when asked for each of them: `ready`, its description; `gone`, `bus.not-found`; `unanswered`, nothing. `asked` is the ids of the resources the registry asks for, and `stillOpen` those open once the checks are done, each compared as a set.

notYetReached.ocaml: OCaml's registry is to run these cases over a scripted knowledge base, as the others do.

cases.why: a knowledge base that does not answer gives no verdict, and every open resource is checked all the same: the gone one closes, and the others stay
a knowledge base that answers as its entry has every open resource checked: the gone one closes, and the others stay
no verdict keeps nothing the knowledge base says is gone: each gone resource closes
